what_it_does: Contains thousands of build recipes, sources, and package outputs outside the current system closure.
reason: The nixos-rebuild and nixos-version manual-page documents: NOT. All other listed store objects: UNKNOWN; names alone do not establish every operational role.

what_it_does: Provides the installed hello executable and its user environment.
reason: The log demonstrates hello executing through the profile; removing this closure prevents that installed program from running.

what_it_does: Supplies an image for the boot menu background.
reason: An image is content; the boot menu theme also falls within the single-program appearance exemption.

what_it_does: Supplies a converted font for boot menu text.
reason: Font appearance is confined to the boot menu; removal loses this visual content rather than the bootloader program.

what_it_does: Contains bootloader modules, configuration, font, translations, and persistent environment.
reason: Loadable modules and their containing directories: MUST; font, translations, and their directories: NOT; all remaining members: UNKNOWN without contents or established use.

what_it_does: Unestablished marker or metadata file.
reason: Only a filename and size are supplied; its contents and consumer are absent.

what_it_does: Records completed directory updates and controls subsequent update-service conditions.
reason: Historical update record suggests exemption; its timestamp controls future services. The text does not resolve operational history versus required behavior.

what_it_does: Empty distribution marker with unestablished consumers.
reason: Inventory shows an empty marker; no evidence establishes what decisions its presence changes.

what_it_does: Runs shell commands when a login shell exits.
reason: Shell-executed logout code has shell rights; the code rule applies even if it contains settings.

what_it_does: Runs commands during shell initialization.
reason: Shell startup files are explicitly required code.

what_it_does: Registers additional executable binary formats in the kernel.
reason: Removing format registrations changes which binaries the operating system can execute; effects extend beyond the configuration reader.

what_it_does: Contains message-bus configuration and service definitions.
reason: Contents and effective policy are absent; service definitions and possible interface-only settings cannot be individually distinguished.

what_it_does: Sets defaults used when creating accounts.
reason: Account creation defaults govern resulting system accounts and rights, rather than only the useradd interface.

what_it_does: Executes shell commands after DHCP client hook processing.
reason: A shell hook executes with interpreter rights and is explicitly required code.

what_it_does: Sets environment variables inherited by user services.
reason: Assignments affect services launched by the manager, not only the manager itself; removing them changes service environments.

what_it_does: Links to a font configuration tree.
reason: Only the directory link is inventoried; target members and their actual settings are unavailable.

what_it_does: Defines filesystems and mount options used by system tools.
reason: Removing mount definitions changes filesystem availability and mount behavior across programs.

what_it_does: Configures userspace filesystem mounting.
reason: File contents are unavailable; cannot establish whether it sets mounting rights or only redundant defaults.

what_it_does: Configures address selection ordering in the shared resolver library.
reason: Shared address-selection rules affect network applications rather than only one program.

what_it_does: Defines groups and their account membership.
reason: Group membership participates in account access rights and superuser authorization.

what_it_does: Configures host resolution through the shared resolver library.
reason: Resolver policy affects multiple programs; removing it changes system name-resolution behavior.

what_it_does: Sets the system host name.
reason: System identity is used across programs, so this is not a setting confined to one program.

what_it_does: Maps host names to network addresses for applications.
reason: Removing mappings changes system name lookup and which named destinations applications can reach.

what_it_does: Configures Readline key bindings used by multiple interactive programs.
reason: The shared library settings govern input in multiple applications; the one-program exemption does not apply.

what_it_does: Supplies text displayed before login.
reason: The login banner is textual content; removing it makes that text unavailable without removing login capability.

what_it_does: Links to keyboard-related resources.
reason: The target tree and its contents are absent; the link name cannot establish the object functions.

what_it_does: Sets system locale defaults inherited by programs.
reason: System-wide language and locale defaults affect multiple programs and are not confined to one interface.

what_it_does: Defines account-management and login defaults.
reason: Account and login rules affect system identities and access; these are explicitly required.

what_it_does: Supplies distribution release identification text.
reason: Release identification is descriptive content; its absence removes that information, not installed capabilities.

what_it_does: Configures logical-volume management.
reason: Actual settings are unavailable; cannot distinguish storage-behavior rules from interface-only preferences or redundant defaults.

what_it_does: Provides persistent system identity used by services and applications.
reason: The identifier supplies system identity across programs; its absence changes identity-dependent behavior and boot initialization.

what_it_does: Configures manual-page utilities and their search paths.
reason: Documentation identifies multiple utilities; saved evidence omits actual settings and consumers, so the one-program exemption and specific removal effects cannot be established.

what_it_does: Configures kernel-module loading, aliases, options, and blacklists.
reason: These settings change kernel behavior and module availability beyond the loading program.

what_it_does: Lists kernel modules to load during boot.
reason: Removing the list changes which kernel code is loaded; effects are not confined to the reader.

what_it_does: Exposes the current mount table through a compatibility path.
reason: Removing the link prevents programs using this path from obtaining mount information; it is operational metadata, not past history.

what_it_does: Supplies text-editor settings and syntax-highlighting preferences.
reason: Nano reads these values as its own settings; the one-program settings exemption applies.

what_it_does: Defines network-wide host and user groups for access rules.
reason: Netgroup data participates in access rules across clients; these are not merely one-program preferences.

what_it_does: Contains package-manager settings and a flake registry.
reason: Neither file contents are saved; cannot establish which system-wide effects, trust rules, or one-program preferences are present.

what_it_does: Specifies system services, boot settings, accounts, and privileges for rebuilding.
reason: These definitions govern the generated system and explicit account privileges; removing them prevents reproduction of that configuration.

what_it_does: Configures the name-service caching daemon.
reason: The format supports logging, cache behavior, and service settings; actual contents are absent, preventing a case-specific exemption decision.

what_it_does: Selects sources and ordering for account and network lookups.
reason: Shared-library lookup rules affect many applications and account resolution; they are not confined to one program.

what_it_does: Supplies operating-system release identification.
reason: Release text describes the installed system; the content exemption applies to that information.

what_it_does: Sets environment values used in authenticated login sessions.
reason: Login environment assignments affect launched sessions and programs, not only the authentication module.

what_it_does: Configures authentication and account checks for login and account-management services.
reason: Authentication policy determines permitted account access and is explicitly required.

what_it_does: Defines user accounts, identities, login shells, and account directories.
reason: Accounts are explicitly required, independently of password-content exemptions.

what_it_does: Provides trusted certificate authorities for TLS authentication.
reason: Removing trusted authorities prevents validation of otherwise trusted connections across applications; these are not account passwords.

what_it_does: Executes shell initialization commands at login.
reason: Shell startup code is explicitly required and executes with shell rights.

what_it_does: Maps protocol names to IP protocol numbers.
reason: Removing the table prevents protocol-name lookup by applications; it is operational input shared across programs.

what_it_does: Selects DNS servers and resolver behavior for applications.
reason: Resolver settings affect system network lookups, not only one program.

what_it_does: Appears to preserve an earlier resolver configuration.
reason: The backup-like name does not establish whether any consumer restores or uses it; contents and use are absent.

what_it_does: Supplies shell-sourced resolver configuration generator settings.
reason: The configuration is sourced by a shell, so the explicit code rule applies even when it holds settings.

what_it_does: Maps RPC program names to RPC service numbers.
reason: Removing the mapping prevents applications from resolving RPC service names; its scope extends across programs.

what_it_does: Maps service names to port numbers and transport protocols.
reason: This shared lookup input enables service-name resolution; removing it makes such lookups unavailable.

what_it_does: Provides shell commands establishing session environment variables.
reason: The generated environment file is shell-executed code; code remains required even when it sets values.

what_it_does: Stores account password verifiers and password-login locking or aging rules.
reason: Password verifiers are exempt, but account locking and password-login permissions are required; the file cannot be omitted wholesale.

what_it_does: Lists permitted login shells for account and access checks.
reason: Programs use this shared list for login-shell selection and access checks; it is system policy.

what_it_does: Contains login keys, server identity keys, known hosts, and client/server settings.
reason: Authorized login key and its containing directories: MUST. Other keys, moduli, known hosts, and configuration members: UNKNOWN without local role or contents evidence.

what_it_does: Exposes certificate-authority bundles and system certificate trust configuration.
reason: System trust determines which remote connections applications authenticate; removing trust inputs disables those validations.

what_it_does: Connects active configuration paths to their generated backing tree.
reason: Many inventoried system configuration links traverse this link; removal makes their targets unavailable and disables configured system behavior.

what_it_does: Authorizes subordinate group ID ranges in child namespaces.
reason: These entries grant account-related identity mapping authority; removing them removes that capability.

what_it_does: Authorizes subordinate user ID ranges in child namespaces.
reason: These entries grant account-related identity mapping authority; removing them removes that capability.

what_it_does: Defines authorization to run commands with elevated privileges.
reason: The right to become superuser is explicitly required.

what_it_does: Sets kernel parameters during boot and network-device initialization.
reason: The settings change kernel behavior outside the reader program, so the single-program exemption does not apply.

what_it_does: Contains service definitions, generators, presets, and several daemon configurations.
reason: Environment generator and its containing directories: MUST. Remaining service trees, presets, and daemon settings: UNKNOWN because local contents and effective behavior are absent.

what_it_does: Provides terminal capability descriptions for terminal-aware applications.
reason: Without the descriptions applications lose supported terminal operations; this is shared operational input rather than display content.

what_it_does: Defines creation, cleanup, ownership, and permissions of runtime filesystem objects.
reason: Rules change files and permissions used by the system, beyond the configuration reader; removal suppresses those actions.

what_it_does: Supplies hardware properties and device-event rules.
reason: Device rules and hardware properties affect system device access and initialization outside the reader program.

what_it_does: Configures the kernel virtual-console keyboard mapping and font.
reason: Settings apply to the shared kernel console rather than only the setup program.

what_it_does: Provides timezone conversion rules used by programs.
reason: Removing timezone rules removes local-time conversion capabilities shared by applications; this is operational data.

what_it_does: Selects the user environment exposing installed commands.
reason: Removing the profile links removes the selected executable environment; the inventory and execution log identify the active installed program.

what_it_does: Makes package expressions available through channel lookup links.
reason: Removing the links prevents package-expression lookup through these configured channels, changing available package-management operations.

what_it_does: Exposes the selected user profile to command search paths.
reason: The execution log uses this profile path to run hello; removing it prevents that command path from working.

what_it_does: Executes editor initialization commands.
reason: Editor configuration in its programming language is explicitly required code, even when commands only configure settings.

what_it_does: Stores a written work note.
reason: The log shows ordinary written document content; removal only loses the note.

what_it_does: Stores compressed logs of package builds.
reason: Build logs are records of the past, explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Contains a garbage-collection lock file.
reason: Inventory establishes the filename but not active locking or consumer state; the effect of removing this instance is unestablished.

what_it_does: Provides the communication socket for the package-management daemon.
reason: Removing the socket prevents clients connecting to the daemon and requesting store operations.

what_it_does: Stores package-store registration metadata and database support files.
reason: Store operations depend on database metadata; database contents are also listed as exempt content. The text does not delimit operational databases from exempt contents.

what_it_does: Protects referenced store paths and dependencies from garbage collection.
reason: Removing roots changes which installed paths the collector preserves, affecting program availability outside the collector.

what_it_does: Selects system generations and package-expression environments.
reason: These links select usable system and package environments; removing them prevents the configured paths from resolving.

what_it_does: Contains a numbered package-builder pool file.
reason: The empty file and number do not establish current locking or allocation effects; no content or consumer evidence is saved.

what_it_does: Caches binary-substitution metadata.
reason: Binary-cache lookup data can be obtained again; removal changes lookup speed rather than available operations.

what_it_does: Records subscribed package-expression channels.
reason: The subscriptions select package-expression sources; removing them prevents updating those configured channels.

what_it_does: Exposes package-expression channels to package lookup.
reason: Removing the channel link prevents expression lookup at the configured path and changes package-management operations.

what_it_does: Links to an administrative package profile.
reason: The inventory supplies the link but no installed target contents; the administrative profile query supplies no packages.

what_it_does: Records completed variable-directory updates and controls update conditions.
reason: Historical update record suggests exemption; its timestamp controls future services. The text does not resolve operational history versus required behavior.

what_it_does: Stores DHCP client identity and lease data.
reason: Identity and lease files are listed without contents or network-server policy; effects of removing these particular values cannot be established.

what_it_does: Records the last login for each account.
reason: Last-login data records past events and is explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Stores account-allocation maps and records of managed accounts.
reason: File names suggest account state, but contents and specific future effects are unavailable; records and active allocation rules cannot be separated.

what_it_does: Stores user lingering, message catalog, random seed, timer history, and clock state.
reason: Linger, seed, clock: MUST; catalog: NOT; timer: HOLE, history versus scheduling; empty coredump and ephemeral-trees: UNKNOWN. Containing directories follow dependencies; outer directory: MUST.

what_it_does: Exposes the runtime lock directory through a compatibility link.
reason: Removing the link prevents applications using the legacy path from sharing their lock files.

what_it_does: Records failed login attempts.
reason: Failed-login records are logs of past events, explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Stores system and user event logs.
reason: Journal entries are logs of past events and are explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Preserves migrated last-login records.
reason: Migrated login history remains a record of the past, explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Records login and logout history.
reason: Login and logout records are past history, explicitly exempt.

what_it_does: Exposes runtime state and communication paths through a compatibility link.
reason: Removing the link makes runtime paths unavailable to programs that use this compatibility location.

what_it_does: Provides directory structure for system, user, cache, service, and temporary files.
reason: Inventory omits directory permissions and consumers; empty or containing directories have different potential roles, preventing a complete member partition.
